html:
Swiss women won the right to vote in federal elections on 7 February 1971, when the male voters approved it in a national referendum by about two to one.

Because changing the constitution needed a vote of the men themselves, the change came late. An earlier referendum in 1959 had failed. Many cantons let women vote locally before 1971, but the small canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden held out until the federal court forced it in 1990.

Elisabeth Kopp became the first woman on the Federal Council in 1984. The late date is often cited as the price of direct democracy, since men were asked to share their own power. Compare Finland in 1906 and the wider movement.
sum: Swiss women won the right to vote in federal elections on 7 February 1971, when the male voters approved it in a national referendum by about two to one.
